item.title: Suspects sought in violent Hilo robbery
item.description: Police are investigating an assault and robbery that occurred at 2 a.m. on Sunday, Jan. 11, in front of a business on the 200 block of Kanoelehua Avenue in Hilo.

item.title: Democrats ask Gabbard to explain presence at FBI raid on election facility
item.description: WASHINGTON (Reuters) — Top Democrats on the Senate and House intelligence committees called on Thursday on Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard to brief their panels on why she was present for an FBI raid on an election facility in Georgia.

item.title: ‘They never give up’: Cowgirls’ second-half rally clinches BIIF DII Girls Basketball Championship
item.description: HILO — During halftime of Wednesday’s KTA/BIIF Division II Girls Basketball Championship, the Kohala Cowgirls found themselves in a hole they needed to dig out of.

item.title: US trade deficit widens despite Trump’s tariffs
item.description: The U.S. trade deficit in goods and services rebounded to $56.8 billion in November, rising 95% from the previous month as President Donald Trump’s tariffs continued to cause huge fluctuations in trade, according to data from the Commerce Department released Thursday.

item.title: Kona Bicycle Day a dream ride for keiki
item.description: KAILUA-KONA — Not long ago, learning to ride a bike was a rite of passage for nearly every child. Neighborhood streets became playgrounds, and a set of wheels meant freedom and independence. Those days have changed.

item.title: US missions to review aid programs for compliance with new rules on abortion, diversity and gender
item.description: The State Department has ordered U.S. missions worldwide to review all aid programs to ensure they meet stringent new rules that prohibit funding of groups working on family planning, diversity or what the Trump administration calls “gender ideology,” according to a cable seen by Reuters. The Trump administration last week announced the expansion of the so-called Mexico City Policy, which opponents call the “global gag rule” because they say it silences abortion rights advocates. item.title: Man accused of squirting Ilhan Omar with vinegar is charged with assault
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS — The man accused of using a syringe to squirt vinegar onto Rep. Ilhan Omar at a community meeting in Minneapolis this week was charged with assault by federal prosecutors Thursday.

item.title: Man with pizza cutter is said to have tried to break Mangione out of jail
item.description: NEW YORK — A man was arrested Wednesday evening after he arrived at a federal jail in Brooklyn impersonating an FBI agent while carrying a pizza cutter and saying he had a court order to release Luigi Mangione, according to a criminal complaint and people familiar with the episode.

item.title: Appeals court rules in favor of protections for Venezuelans
item.description: A federal appeals court in California has ruled that Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem exceeded her authority when she sought to end temporary immigration protections that had allowed hundreds of thousands of people, many of them Venezuelans, to legally live and work in the United States.

item.title: Hawaii visitor arrivals end 2025 well below pre-pandemic peak
item.description: Hawaii ended 2025 with nearly flat visitor arrivals and a tourism economy still short of its pre-COVID peak — and below what many hotels and small businesses say they need to stay afloat.
